questions.question: How many questions are contained in the GOOAQ dataset, and what percentage of mined answers were found accurate in human evaluation?
questions.expected_answer: GOOAQ contains 3 million questions (about 3.1M overall), and human evaluation shows that 94% (94.5% overall) of the mined answers are accurate.
questions.evidence_quote: containing 3 million questions with diverse answer types ranging from factual short answers to snippets to collections. Our human evaluation shows that 94% of the mined answers are accurate

questions.question: During query extraction for GOOAQ, why are questions shorter than 5 tokens filtered out, and what is the average length of the collected questions?
questions.expected_answer: Questions shorter than 5 tokens are filtered out because they are often incomplete questions; the average length of the collected questions is about 8 tokens.
questions.evidence_quote: We filter out any questions shorter than 5 tokens as they are often incomplete questions. This process yields over∼5M questions, which were collected over a span of 6 months. The average length of the questions is about 8 tokens.

questions.question: What qualification requirements were imposed on Amazon Mechanical Turk workers for assessing GOOAQ quality?
questions.expected_answer: Workers had to be based in a predominantly native English-speaking country (USA, Canada, UK, Australia), have completed at least 5000 HITs with >= 99% approval rate, and pass a qualification test of half-a-dozen questions.
questions.evidence_quote: we required workers to be based in a country with a population predominantly of native English speakers (e.g., USA, Canada, UK, and Australia) and have completed at least 5000 HITs with ≥ 99% assignment approval rate. Additionally, we have a qualification test with half-a-dozen questions all of which need to be answered correctly by our annotators.

questions.question: How did the authors of GOOAQ construct training splits to minimize data leakage into the dev and test sets?
questions.expected_answer: They selected the training instances most dissimilar to the evaluation splits, measuring similarity by the maximum token-overlap with any dev/test instance over both questions and answers.
questions.evidence_quote: To minimize this issue, we create training splits by selecting the most dissimilar instances to our evaluation splits. The measure of similarity for each training instance is computed as the maximum amount of tokenoverlap with any of the instances in the test/dev set (computed over both questions and answers).

questions.question: In the PAQ generation pipeline, how are easy negatives and hard negatives sampled to train the RoBERTa passage selection model?
questions.expected_answer: Easy negatives are sampled at random from Wikipedia, while hard negatives are sampled from the same Wikipedia article as the positive passage.
questions.evidence_quote: We sample easy negatives at random from Wikipedia, and hard negatives from the same Wikipedia article as the positive passage. Easy negatives help the model to learn topics of interest, and hard negatives help to differentiate between interesting and non-interesting passages from the same article.

questions.question: Why does PAQ use global filtering with an ODQA model instead of local filtering with a machine reading comprehension model?
questions.expected_answer: Local filtering does not remove ambiguous questions that can only be answered with access to the source passage, whereas global filtering supplies only the generated question without the source passage to ensure consistency.
questions.evidence_quote: However, local filtering will not remove questions which are ambiguous (Min et al., 2020b), and can only be answered correctly with access to the source passage. Thus, we use an ODQA model for filtering, pf (a| q, C), supplied with only the generated question, and not the source passage. We refer to this as global filtering

questions.question: How many filtered QA-pairs are in the final PAQ knowledge base, and from how many extracted answer spans and unique generated questions were they obtained?
questions.expected_answer: PAQ consists of 65M filtered QA-pairs, obtained from 165M extracted answer spans and 279M unique questions before applying global filtering.
questions.evidence_quote: As shown in Table 1, PAQ consists of 65M filtered QA pairs.6 This was obtained by extracting 165M answer spans and generating 279M unique questions before applying global filtering.

questions.question: In selective question answering on Natural Questions, at what answer coverage threshold does FiD outperform RePAQ, and by how much does RePAQ outperform FiD at 50% coverage?
questions.expected_answer: At 50% coverage, RePAQ outperforms FiD by over 10%; FiD only outperforms RePAQ when systems are required to answer more than 85% of questions.
questions.evidence_quote: of 50%, RePAQ outperforms FiD by over 10%. FiD only outperforms RePAQ when we require systems to answer more than 85% of questions.

questions.question: Under what character length or text conditions is a Reddit conversational example filtered out during preprocessing?
questions.expected_answer: An example is filtered out if either the context or response feature has more than 128 characters, fewer than 9 characters, or if its text is [deleted] or [removed].
questions.evidence_quote: The example is filtered if either feature has more than 128 characters, or fewer than 9 characters, or if its text is set to [deleted] or [removed].

questions.question: How is the 1-of-100 accuracy metric defined and computed for conversational response selection?
questions.expected_answer: It is Recall@1 using 99 randomly sampled responses from the test dataset as negatives, efficiently computed in batches of 100 (context, response) pairs where the other 99 elements in the batch act as negatives.
questions.evidence_quote: When evaluating conversational response selection models on these datasets, we propose a Recall@k metric termed 1-of-100 accuracy. This is Recall@1 using 99 responses sampled from the test dataset as negatives.

alternative_gold.evidence_quote: batches of 100 (context, response) pairs can be processed such that the other 99 elements in the batch serve as the negative examples.

questions.question: During the cleaning of SearchQA snippets, what specific terms or attributes caused a snippet to be removed so answers could not be found trivially, and what maximum answer length was retained?
questions.expected_answer: Snippets were removed if they included the air-date of the Jeopardy! episode, the exact copy of the question, or the terms 'Jeopardy!', 'quiz', or 'trivia'; only tuples whose answers were three or less words long were kept.

questions.question: In the 2018 text summarization paper, why does the Lead-3 baseline perform much better on CNN/Daily Mail than on WikiHow, and what ROUGE-L score does Pointer-generator + coverage achieve on WikiHow?
questions.expected_answer: Summarization baselines perform much better on CNN/Daily Mail with Lead-3 outperforming other baselines due to the news inverted pyramid writing style, whereas poor Lead-3 performance on WikiHow reflects the different writing styles in its articles; Pointer-generator + coverage achieves 26.54 ROUGE-L on WikiHow.
questions.supporting_page_quote: As it can be seen, the summarization systems perform a lot better on CNN/Daily mail compared to the WikiHow dataset with lead-3 outperforming other baselines due to the news inverted pyramid writing style described earlier. On the other hand, the poor performance of lead-3 on WikiHow shows the different writing styles in its articles.
